evidence.text: The national cancer roadmap notes that palliative radiotherapy is used less by patients living more than 100 km from the nearest unit, and that outcomes are worse beyond 50 km.

A systematic review of 29 randomised trials in uncomplicated painful bone metastases: a single session relieves pain as well as a multi-session course (61% vs 62% respond), at the cost of more retreatment (20% vs 8%). Guidelines name 8 Gy as the single dose.

FAST-Forward (4,096 patients): 5 sessions in one week is non-inferior to 15 sessions over three weeks, with a similar level of cancer control at 10 years (breast recurrence 2.1% vs 3.6%). Applies to whole breast or chest wall without nodal radiotherapy.
A single 8 Gy session relieves pain as well as a multi-session course, with more retreatment.
5 sessions in one week is non-inferior to 15 sessions over three weeks for eligible patients.
At Turku University Hospital in 2005-2013, only 7% of radiotherapy courses in patients' last year of life were single-session.
Meta-analysis: living 50 km or more from a radiotherapy centre goes with 16% lower odds of receiving palliative radiotherapy (OR 0.84).
Radiotherapy patients often attend daily for several weeks.
Kela paid 364 million euros of travel reimbursement in 2025 for 4.6 million trips; per resident it was highest in Kainuu (157 €) and lowest in Helsinki (23 €).
Patients pay up to 25 € per one-way trip and at most 300 € a year; own-car travel is valued at 0.33 €/km and the overnight allowance is up to 20.18 €.
12 public radiotherapy units serve mainland Finland. Lapland has none: its patients are treated in Oulu.
89 municipalities, home to 637,661 people, are more than 100 km by road from their nearest unit.
For part of the population the nearest central hospital is more than 400 km away and the nearest university hospital more than 700 km.
5,232 women were diagnosed with breast cancer in Finland in 2024 (5,204 on the mainland, excluding Åland).
